player_intent: Players fight the proven Morro do Sol 2v2 demolition layout inside a richer original hillside neighborhood whose foreground reads as constructed architecture, with supplied damaged-plaster and exposed-wood materials, complete glass-and-sash windows, climbable crate staging, supported ramps to both objective-side roofs, smaller occupied buildings stacked above them, monumental clouds, overhead utility lines, dense edge vegetation, and a distant coast.
acceptance_rule: The launcher lists Morro do Sol V1 and V2 separately. V2 preserves every V1 object and every pre-existing V2 non-building transform; replaces the thirty-six disconnected building shell pieces with six base procedural assemblies at the original footprints plus two smaller occupied upper modules; consumes the supplied plaster and wood textures on canonical runtime meshes; constructs glass, sash, mullions, shutters, and bars at every authored window; retains two Alpha spawns, two Bravo spawns, one bomb, A/B sites, the six pre-existing ramps, tall interiors, and no respawns; adds exactly 18 collidable V2 roof-route objects comprising four ramps, two supported landings, four posts, six climb crates, and two upper modules; keeps exactly 51 collision-free tagged art objects and 138 saved objects total; and loads visibly through res://main.tscn.

nodes.role: Builds six base structures and two smaller occupied upper modules with supplied plaster and exposed-wood materials, real door and window voids, glass, sash, mullions, shutters, bars, swinging door leaves, corrugated awnings, physical public-building signs, cornices, pilasters, raised foundations, irregular plaster meshes, exposed brick relief, gutters, downspouts, and electrical service details.

Builds mirrored Alpha and Bravo roof access from collidable timber crate pyramids, two-stage wedge ramps, supported intermediate landings, and smaller occupied upper modules whose ramp endpoints meet the existing terrace and roof heights.
Contains the saved V2 hills, vegetation, exposed framing, cylindrical utility poles, curved overhead cables, and exterior collapse as collision-free map objects.
Renders the stronger blue sky, monumental painted clouds, warm sun, and coastal haze.
Displays the original V2 beach, ocean, green headlands, lower city, and giant cloud beyond the downhill wall without collision.

visual_check: Select Morro do Sol V2 — 2v2 Demolition and enter the canonical Training Range. Inspect the Alpha approach, defender skyline, all eight building facades and interiors, both two-stage roof routes, both crate pyramids, exterior south wall, and ocean-facing view. Confirm supplied plaster and wood are visible on the intended architecture; every window reads as glass, sash, mullions, shutters, and bars; ramps visibly meet their landings and roofs; supports reach the terrace; crates are constructed rather than plain cubes; and presentation-only details do not behave as cover, block aim corridors, hide the reticle, or alter pre-existing routes.
